answer: Each mining identity must post a bond in the network's work-token, slashed if that address proves a duplicate run from one funder device. Since every extra seat needs the same full bond, the marginal delta an attacker pays never shrinks with scale, so a thousand fake miners means a thousand stakes frozen at risk. Sponsorship adds another wall: fresh identities need a vouch from an already-bonded peer who drops in standing if the account is fake, making each new thread of trust carry real liability. A timber-sized heap of accounts costs more than it can harvest, so the attack is unprofitable.
